title: Samsung SDI Debuts Its First Cylindrical LFP Battery for AI Data Center Backup Power
content:
Korea Supply Chain Brief · September 29, 2026

Samsung SDI (KRX: 006400) unveiled its first cylindrical LFP (lithium iron phosphate) battery at Data Center World Asia (DCWA) 2026 in Singapore, part of a broader lineup of backup-power products aimed at AI data centers. Here is what was shown and why data centers are becoming a battery market in their own right.

CompanyRoleEvidence
Samsung SDI
KRX: 006400		Exhibited AI data center battery lineup, including a new cylindrical LFP cellAnnounced (company release, Sep 29, 2026)

What was shown

Samsung SDI set up four exhibit zones at DCWA 2026, an Asia-focused data center industry event that drew about 600 companies this year: uninterruptible power supply (UPS) systems, battery backup units (BBUs), its Samsung Battery Box (SBB) energy storage product, and standalone battery cells.

  • New product: a next-generation cylindrical LFP battery, shown publicly for the first time. Samsung SDI says a proprietary structural design raises output and capacity while improving safety, targeting emergency backup power in AI data centers.
  • UPS fire safety result: a UPS solution that passed all criteria in a large-scale indoor fire test (LSFT) run by UL Solutions, a global safety certification body. The test deliberately burns out a battery module inside a UPS rack to check whether fire spreads to neighboring racks; Samsung SDI said the module burned out but no fire spread, explosion, or rupture occurred in adjacent equipment.
  • BBU zone: a high-output, high-capacity nickel-based (NCM-type) cylindrical battery with a bottom-vent design.
  • SBB zone: a prismatic LFP battery for its "SBB 2.0" all-in-one energy storage system (ESS).

Why data centers are becoming a distinct battery market

AI data centers need backup power that can respond instantly if grid power fails, since even brief outages can disrupt AI training or inference workloads running on expensive accelerator hardware. That is pulling battery makers to design products specifically for this use case rather than repurposing standard ESS or UPS batteries: emphasis on fast discharge response, fire containment within a rack (since data centers pack racks densely), and long cycle life under intermittent backup duty rather than daily deep cycling. Samsung SDI's four-zone lineup — UPS, BBU, SBB, and cell-level products — reflects an attempt to cover the full stack a data center operator would need from one supplier.

Same-day context: Samsung SDI is also an investor in AI infrastructure

On the same day as this product unveiling, Samsung Electronics and five other Samsung affiliates — including Samsung SDI — announced a combined US$1 billion investment in Helix Digital Infrastructure, a KKR-founded company building AI data centers and the power and network infrastructure around them. Samsung Electronics contributed $500 million and the other five affiliates $500 million combined. See our separate brief on the Helix investment for details. The two moves are not described as connected in either release, but they show Samsung SDI positioned on both sides of the AI data center buildout: as a financial investor in infrastructure, and as a supplier of the batteries that infrastructure will use.

What is not disclosed

  • Pricing, capacity specifications (Ah, kWh), or a commercial availability date for the new cylindrical LFP battery.
  • Named customers or supply agreements tied to the products shown at DCWA.
  • Sales or revenue figures for Samsung SDI's data center battery business specifically.

Quick FAQ

What did Samsung SDI show at DCWA 2026?
A four-zone lineup of data center backup batteries: UPS, battery backup units, its SBB energy storage system, and battery cells — including a first-ever public showing of a cylindrical LFP battery.

What is LFP and why does it matter for data centers?
Lithium iron phosphate is a battery chemistry known for thermal stability and safety relative to nickel-based chemistries, which matters for backup power packed densely into data center racks.

Is this related to Samsung's Helix investment announced the same day?
Not stated as connected. Samsung SDI is one of six Samsung affiliates investing in Helix Digital Infrastructure, a separate, financial investment in AI infrastructure announced the same day.
